🚀 kensaku | Rust
🎯 Primary Use Case: To provide users with an extremely fast and comprehensive local file search tool that goes beyond filenames to search document content, image text, and semantic meaning, while maintaining user privacy and offering AI agent integration.
✨ Key Features: • Filename search in milliseconds • Full-text search within documents (PDF, DOCX, EPUB, etc.) • OCR for text extraction from screenshots and images
📖 Summary: Kensaku is a fast, local-first desktop search application built with Rust and Tauri. It allows users to quickly find files by name, content within documents and images (via OCR), and even by semantic meaning. It also integrates with AI agents through the MCP protocol, prioritizing user privacy as nothing leaves the local machine.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

💡 fmx | Rust
🎯 Primary Use Case: To provide a simple, fast, and versatile desktop application for converting various media file types without requiring users to install multiple specialized tools.
✨ Key Features: • All-in-one media conversion (video, audio, image, PDF, eBooks, discs) • Lightweight and fast performance • Simple and intuitive egui GUI • Batch processing and queue management • Right-click integration with file manager
📖 Summary: FMX is a free, open-source media converter built with Rust, offering a user-friendly egui GUI for converting various file types including video, audio, images, documents, and discs. It supports batch processing, system-wide integration via right-click context menus, and provides presets for popular devices and platforms.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

💡 ffmpeg-skill | Python
🎯 Primary Use Case: To empower AI coding agents with a comprehensive, local video editing capability, allowing them to process and manipulate video files directly without external dependencies or data uploads.
✨ Key Features: • 42 FFmpeg tools for video editing (cut, captions, reframe, loudness, etc.)
📖 Summary: ffmpeg-skill provides a local, offline video editing environment for AI coding agents like Claude Code and Cursor. It offers 42 FFmpeg-based tools accessible via a machine-readable contract and an MCP server, enabling agents to perform tasks such as cutting, adding captions, reframing, and loudness normalization without relying on cloud services or API keys.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

🔥 Google-Maps-Scrapper | Python
🎯 Primary Use Case: Automated extraction of business information from Google Maps for analysis and integration into other applications.
✨ Key Features: • Data Scraping from Google Maps listings • Extraction of business name, address, website, contact details • Scraping of review counts and average ratings • Detection of business services (in-store shopping, pickup, delivery) • Extraction of operating hours and introductory information
📖 Summary: This Python repository uses Playwright to scrape business information from Google Maps, extracting details like name, address, website, reviews, and operating hours. It cleans the data and exports it to a CSV file for further analysis.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

🚀 portracker | JavaScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: Real-time network port monitoring and service discovery for self-hosted environments.
✨ Key Features: • Automatic Port Discovery • Platform-Specific Collectors (Docker, TrueNAS) • Internal Port Detection • Lightweight & Self-Contained (SQLite) • Peer-to-Peer Monitoring
📖 Summary: Portracker is an open-source, self-hosted tool that automatically discovers and monitors network ports and services on your systems. It provides a real-time, visual map of your network, helping to prevent deployment issues and eliminate manual tracking.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🚀 browserytools | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: To provide users with a private, convenient, and free suite of browser-based tools for everyday tasks like image editing, file conversion, and AI-powered content processing, all without requiring any uploads or account creation.
✨ Key Features: • 152+ browser-based tools • Client-side processing (no uploads, no accounts, no ads, no tracking)
📖 Summary: BrowseryTools is a collection of 152 free, browser-based utility tools built with Next.js and TypeScript. All file and text processing happens client-side, ensuring privacy with no uploads, accounts, or ads. It includes various tools like image manipulation, PDF converters, and on-device AI functionalities powered by Transformers.js.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source
